pr_title: Fix single threaded seeking not working due to unnecessary seek call
pr_body:
Seeking to `GameplayClock.Time` when calling start - even if the clock is already started - would cause an incorrect second seek, cancelling the user's proposed seek.

I also moved the pause logic here because it seems harmless and feels better.

Closes #11122.

issue_context.title: Seeking gameplay doesn't work in single-threaded execution
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 

Seems like the update of the clock isn't happening as instantaneously as we'd like from `GameplayClockContainer.Seek(time)`, and the following call to `GameplayClockContainer.Start()` seeks back to the original time.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bktoK_Ac1EGFwSGQ1Num9KQ-XqbR4pI6/view?usp=sharing

review_comments:
Just to clarify that I understand the mode of failure correct: this "worked" when multi-threaded but failed single-threaded because in multi-threaded mode enqueued seeks could execute while the update thread was doing its things, making this a race in the multi-threaded case:

```
Update thread						Audio thread

enqueues seek to requested time
									executes enqueued 1st seek
enqueues seek to current time
									executes enqueued 2nd seek
```

and making the first seek a no-op in the single-threaded case (as the second seek reverted it entirely), right?

```
Frame N

update loop enqueues seek to requested time
update loop enqueues seek to current time

Frame N+1

audio thread executes enqueued 1st seek
audio thread executes enqueued 2nd seek <-- reverting 1st seek
```
That's correct, yeah. The audio thread was running so often that it was not an issue in multi-threaded execution.
